headline: ASML lands TSMC and Samsung as High-NA EUV customers; SK Hynix evaluating - $400M-per-tool orders unlock AI-node roadmaps
summary: ASML disclosed that TSMC and Samsung have formally committed to its next-generation High-NA EUV lithography systems, joining Intel as the only three customers on the roadmap. Samsung targets 2028 for DRAM production on High-NA, TSMC 2030 for advanced logic used in AI accelerators. Each tool runs roughly $400M. SK Hynix is still evaluating. Barclays flagged the read-across as visibility-positive: 'Demand is clearly strong.' ASML shares up ~3% in Amsterdam trading.

headline: ASML, TSMC, Samsung and Intel form 12-inch photomask consortium; testing 2031, production 2033 - 40% throughput uplift targeted
summary: Separate from the High-NA order news, ASML announced a joint initiative with TSMC, Samsung and Intel to move from the industry-standard 6-inch to 12-inch photomasks. Larger masks would remove stitching constraints on AI-era die sizes and lift fab productivity ~40%. SK Hynix is evaluating participation. Test fabs slated 2031, production 2033. Long-dated but structurally bullish for equipment intensity per wafer.

headline: Bloom Energy surges ~8% ahead of S&P 500 inclusion Sept 21; UBS lifts target to $325 citing passive-fund absorption
summary: Bloom Energy joins the S&P 500 before the open on Sept 21, replacing Trade Desk in the quarterly rebalance announced Sept 4. Shares climbed roughly 8% Tuesday on the first US session after Labor Day, extending a YTD run above 200% driven by fuel-cell demand from AI datacenter buildouts. UBS raised its price target to $325 from $300, estimating passive vehicles could ultimately hold 10-15% of shares outstanding. Trade Desk fell ~2% on the swap.

headline: SK Hynix jumps ~7% as AI accelerators divert DRAM capacity away from smartphones; HBM4 mix continues to lift blended ASPs
summary: SK Hynix outperformed the KOSPI Tuesday as sell-side notes flagged tightening handset-DRAM supply from HBM4 wafer allocation. Micron held steady while Apple slipped on the mix-shift read. Follows Monday's KB Securities note showing Samsung and SK Hynix DRAM inventory below 10 days as HBM4 consumes 3x conventional wafer capacity per bit. Constructive for HBM leaders, cautionary for handset OEMs.

headline: Micron reportedly targeting ~100K HBM wafers/month by year-end 2026, roughly doubling capacity for Nvidia Vera Rubin ramp
summary: TrendForce and Digitimes report Micron plans to add ~60K wafers/month of HBM capacity to reach 100K/month by end-2026, with 12-high HBM4 slated for ~50% of the mix as it ramps into Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. Samsung and SK Hynix remain 3-4x larger at 150-200K wafers/month each, but Micron is closing the gap. UBS projects SK Hynix retains ~70% of the Rubin HBM4 socket.

headline: Vertiv commits up to $2.6B to build out grid-to-building electrical interconnection for AI datacenters
summary: Vertiv is expanding beyond the datacenter shell into medium- and high-voltage electrical interconnection - substations, switchgear, transformers - to attack the interconnect-queue bottleneck now stretching 5-7 years in US ISO territories. The move slots Vertiv alongside Eaton, ABB and Schneider in the power-side of the AI stack rather than purely thermal/rack-power. Positive for revenue mix but capex-heavy in the near term.

headline: Oracle Q1 FY27 preview: Street models $19.13B / $1.30 EPS Wednesday post-close; options price ~11% move on OCI backlog conversion
summary: Oracle reports fiscal Q1 2027 after the close Wednesday Sept 10. Consensus: $19.13B revenue (+~28% YoY) and $1.30 EPS. Focus items: OCI growth (guided >92% for FY27), conversion cadence on the record $638B RPO, Q2 guide, capex trajectory and any commentary on debt issuance to fund the buildout. Options markets pricing an ~11% post-print move - wide enough that positioning matters.

headline: Snowflake price target raised 50% to $450 by Freedom Broker on AI-workload acceleration read-through
summary: Freedom Broker lifted its Snowflake price target to $450 from $300 (+50%) on Sept 7, one of the widest single-firm revisions of the week. Note cites accelerating AI-workload attach and Cortex/Iceberg monetization. Places Freedom near the high end of the Street range. Watchlist item ahead of the next Snowflake print.

headline: US 10Y yield tops 4.8% on Labor Day reopen; CPI/PPI later this week set the tone for AI-infra multiples
summary: Treasuries reopened weak after Labor Day, with 10Y yields printing above 4.8% intraday before easing - the highest since October 2023. Traders price ~58% odds of a 25bp hike at next week's FOMC after August payrolls came in at 162K (3x expectations). CPI and PPI on deck this week; core CPI expected to slow to 2.4%. Rate-sensitive long-duration AI-infrastructure names (utilities, hyperscaler capex plays) most exposed if yields keep climbing.
